title: Two-week sprint lens: capacity forecasting with skill-burn curves
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Goal: Create a concrete, repeatable two-week sprint forecasting model that translates team-level skill mix into a probabilistic delivery capacity for the cycle. The model will power weekly scope gates and provide a clear, lightweight artifact product teams can use when making scope cuts or swap decisions.

Scope:
- Define 'skill-burn curve' concept: a time-normalized throughput estimate per role (e.g., senior SWE, mid SWE, SWE-IRL, infra eng, product designer, QA) based on historical ticket completion, typical unplanned work, and cross-team coordination overhead.
- Instrument data sources: Linear ticket throughput, on-call time slices, Slack incident summaries, and historical cycle swap logs.
- Produce a spreadsheet + dashboard that shows a probabilistic capacity band for each two-week sprint (P10/P50/P90) and a recommended set of scope-trim suggestions mapped to those bands.
- Integrate into weekly triage cadence: a 15-minute 'Sprint Lens' slot during the planning ritual where PMs and Eng leads review the current capacity band and decide on trims/deferrals.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spreadsheet model can be refreshed with last 12 months of Linear history to produce per-role throughput estimates.
- Dashboard shows P10/P50/P90 capacity for upcoming sprint and highlights >15% deviation from plan compared to baseline.
- Playbook with step-by-step triage protocol written and approved by at least three ENG leads and two PMs.

Tradeoffs and design notes:
- We intentionally prefer a lightweight probabilistic model over a heavyweight ML prediction to keep ownerability with PMs. That allows manual overrides for known context (major launches, hiring lags).
- We trade off granularity of ticket-level estimation for roll-up accuracy by focusing on historical completion rates and role-level multipliers instead of per-ticket effort estimation.
- To reduce noisy signals, we apply a rolling 8-week exponential decay to older data when estimating current skill-burn curves.

updates: 2026-01-12: Kickoff meeting with ENG leads (Alice, Marco, Priya) + PM guild. Agreed scope and P50 baseline approach.
2026-01-18: Pulled 12 months of Linear throughput exports; started role mapping (senior/mid/junior, infra, design, QA). Initial data cleaning notes attached in spreadsheet.

2026-01-26: First-pass skill-burn curves generated; observed large variance in mid-level SWE throughput between infra-heavy squads and product squads — added normalization factor for cross-team dependencies.

2026-02-02: Prototype dashboard wired to CSV export; validated P50/P90 bands against last three sprints, discrepancies flagged (incidents impact). Decided to include an 'incident tax' adjustment variable.
2026-02-05: Playbook draft ready for 1st review. Requested feedback from Design (for UI of the dashboard) and Solutions Eng (for Dedicated customer impact scenarios).
next_steps: 1) Run pilot with three teams next sprint (infra-core, embeddings team, Console UX) and collect pilot feedback. 2) Finalize playbook edits and add triage checklist. 3) Automate weekly CSV refresh and dashboard update via scheduled job. 4) Build small feature in Console rollout page to show Sprint Lens P-band when choosing rollout windows.
blockers: Data quality: inconsistent ticket labeling across teams (epic vs subtask). Need tagging guidelines & a one-off retro-cleanup for pilot teams. Also blocked on dashboard access for two ENG leads pending Okta group grant.
review_notes: Requested that ENG leads verify rolling decay parameter (currently 8 weeks) and confirm whether incident tax should be additive or multiplicative. PM guild asked for a short 'how to use' video to accompany the playbook.
owner_acknowledgement: Liam O'Connor — I will own pilot coordination and iterate playbook with squad leads. Target to present results at Product Review on 2026-03-05.
notes_for_engineering: When automating CSV refresh, ensure we throttle exports to avoid hitting rate limits on Linear API. Add a snapshot table to the planning DB to prevent time-of-query skew. Consider adding a webhook that triggers on incidents to update 'incident tax' in near real-time.
implementation_risks: If hiring/intern ramp exceeds historical patterns, the model will underforecast capacity until recalibrated. Manual override rules must be prominent in the playbook. Overreliance on the model for scope cuts without qualitative context could underdeliver on commitments.
communication_plan: 1) Pilot announcement to squads + calendar invites for Sprint Lens reviews. 2) One-pager to execs summarizing approach & expected benefits (reduced mid-cycle de-scopes, faster decisioning). 3) Post-pilot writeup with quantitative metrics: % reduction in emergency scope cuts, accuracy of P50 vs realized throughput.
estimated_impact: Improved short-cycle predictability: target a 25% reduction in mid-sprint scope churn for pilot squads and a 10% increase in on-time completion for committed scope across pilot teams.
